elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) impose substantively identical caps on IBM and Customer, respectively.

elements.element: The capped fees measure includes fees both paid and payable.
elements.evidence: The cap refers only to “charges paid by Customer to IBM”; it does not include charges payable but not yet paid.

elements.element: The capped fees measure uses the 12 months preceding the applicable claim.
elements.evidence: The clause measures charges during the 12 months preceding “the accrual of the first claim related to the Services,” rather than the 12 months preceding the applicable claim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable fees measure and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The greater-of floor is $100,000, not USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Special, incidental, indirect and consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “either party” will not be liable to the other for special, incidental, indirect or consequential damages, subject to the stated payment exception.

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's breach of confidentiality obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: New subsection 9(d) provides that the caps in 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) do not apply to damages arising from “a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's breach of data protection obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses data protection obligations.

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's breach of security obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses security obligations.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification payments under Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are listed separately in subsections 9.1(a) and 9.2(a), while the caps apply to “other actual direct damages” under 9.1(c) and 9.2(c).

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's gross negligence are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection 9(d) expressly disapplies both parties' caps to damages arising from “gross negligence.”

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's wilful misconduct are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection 9(d) expressly disapplies both parties' caps to damages arising from “willful misconduct.”

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's fraud are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is not included in the carve-outs.

elements.element: Damages arising from a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property are uncapped.
elements.evidence: No express carve-out covers infringement of the other party's intellectual property; the referenced indemnification provisions cannot be assumed to cover this requirement.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause says Section 10 does not apply to Customer's failure to pay, but it neither states that payment obligations are not damages nor expressly excludes them from the caps in 9.1(c) and 9.2(c).

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) impose substantively identical liability-cap formulas on IBM and Customer.

elements.element: The mutual cap is limited to 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of $100,000 and 12 months of charges paid. When 12 months of charges are below $100,000, the cap exceeds 12 months' fees.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification payments are addressed separately in 9.1(a) and 9.2(a), while the caps in 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) apply to “other actual direct damages.”

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's breach of confidentiality obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection 9(d) expressly disapplies both parties' caps to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's gross negligence are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection 9(d) expressly disapplies both parties' caps to gross negligence.

elements.element: Damages arising from either party's wilful misconduct are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection 9(d) expressly disapplies both parties' caps to willful misconduct.

result.reason: The added mutual carve-out successfully places confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the direct-damages caps, and indemnification payments are structurally outside those caps. However, neither level is complete: the preferred $1,000,000 floor, paid-or-payable measure and several carve-outs are absent, while the fallback cap is not limited to 12 months' fees because of the operative $100,000 floor. The payment proviso also does not expressly remove payment obligations from the Section 9 caps. The added sentence is intelligible, but the rendered clause is fragmented, contains duplicated lettering and incomplete surrounding provisions, reducing drafting quality.
